answer: Fiber-optic acoustic crosstalk tomography binds nodes to unique optical transceiver bundles. Nodes pulse coordinated 1550 nm signals across physical fiber strands, recording inter-core acoustic backscatter on adjacent channels. Each candidate processes this return with an opal dispersion matrix, yielding non-repeatable phase shifts. A grove of validator nodes aggregates these matrix traces to mirror routing topology against actual fiber delays. Simulating 10,000 fake identities requires 48,000 GPU-hours and 9.4 million dollars in dedicated interferometers.
